business_scope.primary_industry_name: Delivery-Only Multi-Brand Cloud Kitchen Facility Operations

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Luxembourg (unitary national jurisdiction, no sub-state tax distinction)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (French/Napoleonic tradition; unitary national system with EU-law primacy)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union (TFEU, Articles 49 and 54, freedom of establishment)
Luxembourg - United States Double Taxation Convention (1996, as amended by the 2004 and 2009 Protocols)
OECD Multilateral Instrument (MLI) for BEPS, signed 2017
New York Convention on the Recognition and Enforcement of Foreign Arbitral Awards (1958)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law of 12 November 2004 on the fight against money laundering and terrorist financing, as amended by the Laws of 13 February 2018, 25 March 2020 and 27 October 2020 (transposing EU Directive 2018/843/AMLD5); Law of 13 January 2019 establishing the Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE), implemented by the Grand-Ducal Regulation of 24 January 2019 and administered by the Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR); CSSF Regulation 12-02 as amended; Law of 10 August 1915 on commercial companies; Luxembourg Criminal Code (Articles 506-1 et seq.).
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_disclosure_level: Government_Only_Access (RBE access is restricted: competent authorities, the Luxembourg financial intelligence unit (CRF), credit and financial institutions, notaries and other obliged entities have statutory access; third parties must demonstrate a legitimate interest to the LBR; no unrestricted public search is available for ghost-kitchen or online-delivery counterparties)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of passport of each founder and UBO (identity page)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent national passport authority or police registry of the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization (country of origin)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Original good-standing certificate and certificate of incorporation of each corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Commercial registry or company register of the shareholder's home jurisdiction

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Police clearance certificate (bulletin n°3 equivalent) of each proposed gérant (day-to-day manager) and UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Ministry of Justice or national criminal records office of the country of residence

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized proof of residential address and bank reference letter of each founder (utility bill or bank statement issued within the preceding 3 months)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Utility company or regulated bank of the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization (unless an EU-regulated mobile ID is accepted by the notary)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory layered screening of all UBOs, gérants, signatories and beneficial owners against: (a) EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, including solidarity lists; (b) UN Security Council Consolidated List; (c) US OFAC SDN list; (d) Luxembourg national and CSSF sanction measures; (e) PEP registers, national and international, with adverse-media and negative-news checks; and (f) platform-triggered aggregator KYC requirements for the UberEats and DoorDash payout rails. Screening must be repeated on a rolling 12-month basis under Article 3-3 of the 2004 AML Law, evidenced in the customer due diligence file, and retained for at least five years after the termination of the business relationship.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) - Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) electronic platform at www.lbr.lu, accessed directly or through guichet.lu
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names are governed by Article 109 of the Law of 10 August 1915 on commercial companies and by the distinguishability provisions of the Law of 19 December 2002 on the register of commerce and companies. French is the predominant statutory drafting language; non-Latin-script names must be transliterated into a French-language phonetic equivalent in the articles of association (statuts) and in the RCS recordal. The name must be distinguishable from pre-existing RCS names, must not be contrary to public order, and must be followed by the legal-form token 'Société à Responsabilité Limitée' or 'SARL' or 'S.à r.l.'. The word 'Luxembourg' or any translation thereof in the name requires prior authorization from the Ministry of the Economy under the Law of 9 June 2017.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: BANQUE / BANCA / BANK - requires prior CSSF authorization
ASSURANCE / INSURANCE / RÉASSURANCE - requires prior CAA (Commissariat aux Assurances) authorization
FONDS / FUND / OPC / SICAV / SICAR - requires CSSF licensing and is prohibited for an operational SARL
FINANCE / FINANCIÈRE / CRÉDIT - requires ministerial clearance and risks misdescribing the licensed activity
LUXEMBOURG / LËTZEBUERG - requires Ministry of the Economy authorization under the Law of 9 June 2017
GHOST KITCHEN / CLOUD KITCHEN - accepted only as descriptive terms that do not create confusion with food-safety licensing or platform-authorization status
STATE / GRAND-DUCHY / ROYAL / NATIONAL - reserved designations requiring State authorization
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Name reservation is filed electronically by the notary or legal counsel at the LBR and is valid for 30 calendar days; a single renewal may be requested before expiry, otherwise a fresh reservation is required. Upon RCS rejection, a revised name should be reserved within 3 business days. If the rejection is contested, the applicant files an administrative objection with the RCS Registration Officer under the Law of 19 December 2002; if the Registration Officer upholds the refusal, the applicant may seize the Tribunal d'arrondissement de Luxembourg (district court) within 3 months of notification by a writ served by a Luxembourg huissier de justice, following the contentious administrative procedure with the State Public Prosecutor (Parquet) and with all pleadings in French.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Conditionally permissible for the statutory registered seat: a SARL may be registered at a private address, at the manager's residence, or at the office of a CSSF-approved domiciliation agent under the Law of 31 May 1999 on the domiciliation of companies. However, for ISIC 5610 ghost-kitchen operations the RCS and obliged entities expect a demonstrable operational address; a pure virtual office without an ALVA-approved kitchen lease or local delivery-market evidence triggers enhanced due diligence by the notary and banks and creates sham-incorporation risk. Recommended path: main registered office at the operating kitchen address, or at an approved agent's office coupled with a separate ALVA-registered operating site.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: HIGH (estimated 60% within the first 12 months of operations): ALVA (Autorité luxembourgeoise de sécurité alimentaire) conducts unannounced hygiene and establishment inspections of delivery-only kitchens under EU food-hygiene rules; the commune's commercial-license authority and the CCSS/ITM may perform on-site controls; the RCS/LBR does not physically inspect at incorporation, but any material-change filing without corresponding operational substance is flagged under the 2004 AML Law.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Name reservation and availability check at the RCS/LBR
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR), Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Fixed statutory tariff applicable to the electronic filing under the fee schedule of the Law of 19 December 2002

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarial deed of incorporation (acte notarié de constitution) at minimum capital of EUR 12,000
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Luxembourg notary (notaire) appointed by the founders
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory notarial tariff per the Grand-Ducal Regulation of 5 June 2020, calculated on subscribed capital with minimum notarial fee, plus registration formalities

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Legal drafting of statutes (statuts), shareholders' resolutions and the corporate KYC file
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Law firm admitted to the Luxembourg Bar
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market rate of EUR 300 to 450 per hour for corporate counsel (4 to 6 hours budgeted)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: AML/CFT customer due diligence and UBO piercing research package per identified UBO and gérant
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: External AML compliance consultant or notary KYC service
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark for CSSF Regulation 12-02-aligned screening, including PEP, sanctions, and adverse-media checks

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Apostille and consular legalization of four foreign KYC documents (passports, police clearances, good-standing certificates)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Competent Ministries of Foreign Affairs and Consulates of the countries of origin
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory and consular per-document fees prevailing in the origin states under the Hague Apostille Convention (90-day validity)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Certified French translation of apostilled foreign corporate and identity documents
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Sworn translator (expert-traducteur) enrolled with the Luxembourg district court
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Judicial per-page tariff, market benchmark of approximately EUR 65 per notarial extract

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Criminal-record certificates (bulletin n°3) of the two proposed gérants
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Ministry of Justice of Luxembourg (Casier judiciaire national)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory fee of EUR 30 per certificate, issued directly to the notary

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Final RCS registration recordal and RESA electronic publication after the notarial deed
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (RCS) and the consolidated journal RESA (Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Official recordal fee of approximately EUR 40, with publication effected by the notary at no separate charge

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: UBO declaration submission to the RBE (Register of Beneficial Owners)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory processing is free of charge and is included in the notary's filing workflow

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered-office domiciliation service at a CSSF-approved agent - first quarter
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Commercial market benchmark of EUR 250 to 350 per month, invoiced quarterly in advance

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Initial professional liability and food-delivery operation pre-cover (interim civil liability of the SARL)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Insurance market benchmark for a low-risk standard food-delivery facility covering the first three months, subject to final underwriting

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, as amended (Titre II – Société à responsabilité limitée, Articles 181–216); Law of 19 December 2002 on the register of commerce and companies; RESA publication rules
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), operational through MyRCS electronic filing portal
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Authentic deed of incorporation (acte constitutif) and articles of association (statuts) executed before a Luxembourg notary
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Minimum statutory capital for a SARL is EUR 12,000; the entire capital must be subscribed and fully paid up before incorporation. Cash contributions must be deposited into a blocked account (compte bloqué) with a Luxembourg credit institution and may be released only after RCS registration. Contributions in kind require a report by an independent auditor (réviseur d'entreprises).
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the sole shareholder approves and confirms the subscription of the entire share capital of the company, being one hundred shares with a nominal value of EUR 120.00 each, totalling EUR 12,000, fully paid up by cash into the company’s blocked account; RESOLVED FURTHER, that the registered office of the company be and is hereby fixed at [registered address] in Luxembourg and adopted for all legal and administrative purposes; RESOLVED FURTHER, that [Name] be and is hereby appointed as manager (gérant) with sole signature authority; that this appointment takes effect immediately; and that the manager is hereby authorised to register the company with the RCS, open corporate bank accounts and take all steps necessary to obtain operating licences.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate name clearance and object verification
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – MyRCS online portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the proposed legal name (including at least one alternative) and the concise corporate object through MyRCS. The name must include the suffix 'S.à r.l.' and must not conflict with existing registered names or protected rights. Wait for RCS approval; incorporate the cleared name into the draft articles.
required_dossiers: Identification documents of founders and manager
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected, the RCS provides a reasoned notice; founders may promptly submit alternative name proposals. Rejection is cured by filing revised name applications and obtaining clearance before notarisation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening of blocked share capital escrow account
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg credit institution under CSSF supervision
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a blocked account in the name of the company being formed at a Luxembourg bank. Deposit EUR 12,000 in cash. Obtain the bank's blocking certificate (attestation de blocage) stating the funds are irrevocably reserved and will be released only upon presentation of the RCS registration certificate. Deliver the certificate to the notary.
required_dossiers: Passport or ID of shareholder and manager
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank queries KYC or source of funds, supply further documentary evidence. The notarisation cannot proceed until the bank issues a valid blocking certificate; remedying the query restarts the SLA upon submission of complete documentation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Chambre des Notaires du Luxembourg – notary designated by the founders
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Provide the notary with the final draft statuts, bank blocking certificate, and KYC documentation. All shareholders must appear before the notary, either personally or by notarised proxy. The notary verifies legality, legal capacity, capital payment, and governance terms, then executes the authentic deed. The notary files the deed with RCS.
required_dossiers: Final articles of association signed by all shareholders
Passports / identity cards of shareholders and manager
Proof of residence and KYC forms
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary identifies a legal deficiency, the draft articles are amended and the deed is re-executed in a subsequent session. Rectification does not require a new capital deposit unless the capital amounts or shareholders change.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration with the Luxembourg Trade Register (RCS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The notary transmits the authenticated deed of incorporation and the filing request via the RCS electronic interchange. RCS verifies compliance, registers the company, and issues an RCS extract and national business number. Legal personality becomes effective upon registration.
required_dossiers: Payment confirmation of RCS registration fee
List of managers and their powers
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry issues a reservation or query, answer in writing within the stated deadline. If the defect is material, the notary executes a corrective deed and refiles; the original application remains suspended until cured.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Recueil Électronique des Sociétés et Associations (RESA) – official Luxembourg electronic publications
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After RCS registration, the notary or the RCS requests publication of the incorporation particulars in RESA. The publication ensures opposability to third parties. Once published, an original certified copy of the deed is returned to the company.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the publication is defective or omitted, submit a corrected publication request to RESA/LBR. The initial registration date remains effective, and a correcting publication is issued free of prejudice to the company's legal personality.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD); Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT); Centre Commun de la Sécurité Sociale; Guichet.lu single window
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Using the RCS extract, file via Guichet.lu to obtain the national identification number, VAT number, corporate income tax file, and, if hiring staff, employer registration with the Centre Commun de la Sécurité Sociale. Register the kitchen facility for occupational health supervision with the Inspection du Travail et des Mines (ITM) as required.
required_dossiers: RCS extract (extrait du registre de commerce)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If any tax or social security registration is rejected for incomplete information, resubmit after correcting the documentation. Late filings may trigger administrative fines but are cured by subsequent compliance with the issuing authority.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of the Economy – General Directorate for Industry, acting through the Guichet.lu single window; municipal business licensing department for the commune of registered office; food safety approval through the competent health inspection service
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Establishment authorisation (autorisation d'établissement) for the operation of a food business, together with health registration/approval under Regulation (EC) No 852/2004 and any commune occupation permit for the ghost kitchen site

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Administration de l'Environnement – Luxembourg Environment Agency
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Registration (class 9 of Annex II to the amended Grand-Ducal Regulation of 15 May 2018 on environmental impact assessment); not a full EIA report for a delivery-only ghost kitchen facility below the thermal and waste discharge thresholds. An environmental registration notice must be filed before works commence.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater discharges must comply with municipal sewer ordinance limits (pH 6–9, BOD/COD and suspended solids thresholds); grease separators and oil retention devices are mandatory. Kitchen exhaust air must meet the standards for particulate, odours and gas emissions under Luxembourg clean-air regulations, including maintenance of grease filters and extraction stack testing. Waste oil, packaging and biowaste must be sorted and collected by certified waste operators in accordance with the Law of 21 March 2017 on waste obligations.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Before opening, the facility must obtain a fire safety clearance from the competent municipal fire protection service, including emergency exit signage, extinguisher location and kitchen exhaust fire-suppression testing; a structural load inspection certificate for cooking equipment, ovens and extraction systems; and occupational health and safety registration with the Inspection du Travail et des Mines (ITM), including affiliation with the accident insurance association and a workplace inspection report.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD) for direct taxes; Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) for VAT. Central portal: MyGuichet.lu / guichet.lu.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A Luxembourg-resident SARL obtains its corporate income tax NIF automatically upon registration with the Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés. For VAT, the SARL must file Form 506 (VAT registration application) via MyGuichet with the Administration de la TVA, indicating estimated taxable turnover. A foreign entity without a Luxembourg establishment must appoint a Luxembourg fiscal representative (représentant fiscal) and submit the registration application through that representative; no registration threshold applies to non-resident suppliers. The VAT number is issued in the format LU00000000 prior to commencing Luxembourg taxable activities.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Luxembourg has no check-the-box election. Available statutory mechanisms: (i) tax consolidation (fiscal unity) under Article 164bis LIR; (ii) VAT grouping under Article 59 of the VAT Law; (iii) option to waive the small-business VAT exemption; (iv) participation exemption election under Article 166 LIR for qualifying shareholdings; (v) application of hybrid mismatch rules under ATAD as implemented by Luxembourg law.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 35,000 annual taxable turnover for resident small businesses (VAT exemption); non-resident entities have no threshold and must register before supplying goods/services in Luxembourg; intra-Community distance sales subject to OSS threshold of EUR 10,000.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No mandatory real-time fiscal clearance, continuous transaction control, or digital stamping for B2B/B2C VAT invoices in Luxembourg. VAT returns (Form 102) must be filed electronically via MyGuichet on a monthly or quarterly basis depending on turnover. E-invoicing is mandatory in the B2G sector through the PEPPOL network. All invoices must comply with EU VAT invoicing rules and be retained for 10 years.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating of 0% VAT applies to supplies of goods physically dispatched or transported outside the EU by the supplier or on behalf of the customer. The customer must establish non-EU status and the goods must leave the EU territory within the statutorily accepted timeframe (generally within 90 days or the transport document validity). For a ghost kitchen, export zero-rating is limited to physical meal/consumer goods sold to non-EU customers with adequate transport evidence; offshore services to non-EU recipients may be outside the scope of Luxembourg VAT if the recipient is a business and the service is effectively used outside the EU. The taxpayer must retain full documentary evidence of export movement and the non-EU business status of the customer.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Bill of Lading / CMR / Air Waybill or equivalent transport document
Inward Remittance Certificate or equivalent bank/payment evidence showing receipt of export proceeds from the non-EU customer
Commercial invoice / proforma invoice matching the export declaration
Proof of non-EU customer status (e.g., contract, order, country of establishment)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The Luxembourg tax authorities may deny zero-rating where documentary evidence is incomplete or fraudulent, and issue additional VAT assessments at the standard 17% rate. Late-payment interest accrues at 0.6% per month on the underdeclared amount. Administrative fines of up to EUR 250,000 or double the evaded tax may be imposed for deliberate VAT evasion, with criminal liability in cases of fraud. Input VAT deductions originally claimed against the zero-rated export may be retrospectively clawed back. The standard limitation period for VAT assessments is five years, extending to ten years in fraud situations.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL), operating within the European System of Central Banks and in coordination with the Luxembourg Ministry of Finance and the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF) for prudential and AML matters.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The euro is fully convertible. Luxembourg imposes no exchange controls on capital or current account transactions pursuant to Article 63 TFEU and applicable OECD/EU liberalisation codes. Profit repatriation, intercompany payments and liquidation proceeds are freely remittable, subject only to standard AML/KYC diligence, proper corporate authorisation and statutory withholding tax at 15% or treaty-reduced rates for non-resident shareholders.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There is no statutory surrender, foreign-exchange conversion or holding-period rule for export proceeds in Luxembourg. EUR and non-EUR export receipts are freely creditable to the company's bank accounts; the bank may require the standard balance-of-payments statistical declaration to the BCL for material cross-border receipts.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banque et Caisse d'Épargne de l'État, Luxembourg (BCEE)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational current account and capital subscription/blocked account linked to the full subscription of SARL share capital.
Multicurrency operational account with dedicated escrow capabilities for initial capital injection and treasury operations.
Operational and multicurrency current account, with integrated trade finance and liquidity-management facilities for small and mid-cap corporate clients.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium. A Luxembourg or EEA-licensed Electronic Money Institution (EMI) or Payment Institution can support multi-platform payouts, API-driven foreign-currency settlement and lower-cost cross-border transfers; however, an EMI cannot replace the physical bank needed for statutory capital escrow, notarised contributions, credit lines or documentary trade finance. Offshore digital EMIs without EEA passporting are Low viability and will be rejected by Luxembourg clearing banks because they lack correspondent bank sponsorship and regulatory equivalence.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: A managing director or duly authorised corporate officer must normally appear physically before the onboarding bank for the first KYC interview, or provide a video-call interview with an identical passport image combined with a notarised, apostilled and certified copy of corporate documents. Remote-only account opening is not generally accepted for a non-resident owner-managed ghost kitchen SARL; the bank may relax physical appearance where the 25% or more UBO is an established EU financial institution or regulated entity and full source-of-funds evidence is provided.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Ghost kitchen has no publicly visible storefront and operates exclusively as a virtual brand on UberEats, DoorDash and similar delivery platforms, creating an ambiguity around physical operational location.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Lease or registered virtual-office agreement for the commercial kitchen site; food handling / municipal operating licence; delivery platform merchant registration screenshots; utility bills; photographs and CCTV inventory of the kitchen; Luxembourg RCS commercial register excerpt; VAT registration certificate; and the company's projected transaction-flow statement.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-volume, low-value micro-payments arriving from multiple international food aggregator intermediaries create a pattern inconsistent with the company's declared headcount or supply-chain expenses.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed UberEats/DoorDash payout agreements; platform settlement reports showing gross and net amounts; internal reconciliation and treasury policy; merchant fee invoices; payroll and supplier bank statements; quarterly VAT and CIT returns; and an auditor-prepared fundraising/operational cash-flow projection.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident directors or ultimate beneficial owners are located outside the EU/EEA, for example the United States or Asia, increasing third-country AML risk exposure.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified colour copy of valid passports; residence permits or utility bills confirming current address; UBO declaration under Luxembourg law; source-of-wealth documentation such as bank statements, investment portfolios and sale-and-purchase agreements; professional reference letters from regulated legal, tax or financial advisers; and signed oath / sworn affidavit where the bank so requests.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: An offshore brand-owner or IP-licensing company resident in a zero-tax or fast-track jurisdiction is receiving royalty or management fees from the Luxembourg SARL, raising transfer-pricing and beneficial-ownership questions.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed IP/brand licence or franchise agreement; substance evidence of the licensor (premises, personnel, decision-making board minutes); international IP valuation or benchmarking study; OECD-compliant transfer-pricing documentation; intercompany invoice ledger with VAT treatment; CbC report references; and evidence of actual services or technology provided.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Use a SEPA Credit Transfer (within the EEA) or SWIFT MT103 for non-EEA investors, with ISO purpose code 'INVE' or 'EQUI' captioning the transfer as share capital subscription. The beneficiary IBAN must be the SARL's blocked/subscription account; the payment reference must recite the RCS registration number, the notarial deed date and the subscribed capital amount. The receiving bank will file with the BCL a direct investment declaration where the transaction falls within BOP statistical thresholds. For non-EUR capital payments, the investor must remit to an approved currency account or convert spot at the receiving bank after funds clear; tagged inward credit verification is mandatory for the notary's capital confirmation.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Clearing rails are: (i) SEPA Credit Transfer and SEPA Instant Credit Transfer for euro-denominated suppliers, salary payments, rent and logistics costs within the EEA; (ii) SWIFT MT103 with gpi tracking for non-EEA trade settlements, royalty remittances and brand-licence fees; (iii) Commercial Letters of Credit (MT700, MT707) with deferred or sight drafts for significant imported food equipment or bulk raw-material purchase orders requiring exporter security; and (iv) intercompany cash-pooling through the host bank using zero-balancing or notional pooling structures, supported by executed intercompany loan agreements and an arm's-length interest policy.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Spot EUR//USD transactions executed through the opening Luxembourg bank for fee and settlement purposes
Plain-vanilla EUR//USD forward contracts with a maturity not exceeding 12 months
EUR//CNY, EUR//GBP or EUR//USD non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) used solely for cash-flow hedging of platform settlements and Chinese/UK supply-chain costs
Cross-currency interest-rate swaps (CCIRS) on intercompany loans exceeding EUR 1,000,000
FX swaps or rolled forwards for short-term working-capital and liquidity clearing positions
Zero-premium collar / forward-band structures for hedging the core brand royalty and distribution margin against USD volatility

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual general meeting (AGM) and minutes approving annual accounts, profit allocation and release (quitus) of the gérants
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Internal governance record kept at the registered office; resolutions amending the articles or capital are filed with the RCS within 1 month
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months after the financial year-end (e.g., 30 June for a 31 December FYE); postponement requires a reasoned collective resolution
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: No direct administrative fine; any shareholder may petition the commercial court to order the meeting; unapproved accounts block the RCS annual filing and expose managers to director liability

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual accounts (comptes annuels) — balance sheet, profit and loss and annexes — filed at the RCS
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers — Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 7 months of the financial year-end (e.g., 31 July for a 31 December FYE); electronic filing required; publication in RESA follows
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Court-ordered compliance procedure at the instance of any interested party or the public prosecutor; administrative fines up to €2,500 and daily coercive fines; persistent default triggers compulsory judicial liquidation/strike-off (radiation) of the SARL

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual confirmation of the register of beneficial owners (Registre des bénéficiaires effectifs — RBE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 1 month after the anniversary date of the company's RBE initial registration; the RBE's annual reminder indicates the exact confirmation deadline
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-confirmation: fine of €250–€1,250 per infringement; knowingly false UBO declarations: imprisonment of 6 months–5 years and/or fine up to €125,000; individuals and legal representatives held personally liable

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual VAT return (déclaration annuelle de TVA) in addition to monthly/quarterly Luxembourg VAT returns
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By 1 May of the year following the calendar year (e.g., 1 May 2026 for FY 2025); monthly returns fall due by the 20th day of the month following the period
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty up to €250 and late-payment interest of 0.6% per month; additional 10% surcharge may apply to VAT assessed ex officio

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax (IRC), municipal business tax (ICC) and net wealth tax (IFL) return and assessment exposure
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD) — Luxembourg Inland Revenue
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By 31 December of the year following the tax year (e.g., 31 December 2026 for FY 2025); discretionary extensions may be granted on written request; quarterly prepayments of taxes fall due on 10 February, 10 May, 10 August and 10 November
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing fines up to €5,000 and/or 10% surcharge on the tax due; late-payment interest of 0.6% per month; ACD may assess income ex officio where books are absent

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Minimum net wealth tax (impôt sur la fortune) — the Luxembourg franchise-equivalent charge for SARLs
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual flat tax of €35 for small SARLs (balance sheet total ≤ €350,000); €1,605 minimum where financial fixed assets exceed €350,000; due with the CIT/IFL return by 31 December following the tax year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Interest at 0.6% per month from the statutory due date; enforced collection by distraint; failure to file triggers an ex officio assessment of the applicable minimum

stage_6.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Statutory tax holidays or preferential deductions
